# Pipeline & Contact Details

##Medical imaging pipeline

**Object → Device → Raw data → Algorithm → Reconstructed image**

## Anatomical plans

| Map | Separates | Etymology |
|------|--------|-----------|
| **Axial** (= transverse) | Sup/Inf | — |
| **Sagittal** | Left / Right | *sagitta* = arrow |
| **Coronal** | Ant/Post | *corona* = crown |

## Coordinate codes

| Letter | Management |
|--------|-----------|
| S/I | Upper / Lower |
| L/R | Left / Right |
| A/P | Anterior / Posterior |

⚠️ Left/Right = **patient’s point of view**

💡 Example: **LSA** → x: L→R, y: S→I, z: A→P (used in CT)

# Terms — Overview

| Modality | Vector | Type |
|----------|---------|------|
| **Ultrasound (US)** | High frequency pressure waves | Reflection |
| **X-ray / CT** | Ionizing radiation | Transmission |
| **SPECT / PET** | Metabolic emission Broadcast |
| **MRI (MRI)** | Nuclear spin precession | Magnetic resonance |

## Anatomical vs. Functional

| | Anatomical | Functional |
|-|-----------|------------|
| Modality | MRI, CT, X-ray | PET, fMRI, SPECT |
| Watch | Physical structure | Physiological activity |
| Deceased patient | Same image | Black image (PET) |

# Data types

| Dimensions | Structure | Modality |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| **1D** | Scalar value | ELISA, fluorescence, sequencing |
| **2D** | Pixel matrix | X-ray |
| **2D series** | 3D tensor (x,y,t) | Fluoroscopy, video |
| **2D color** | 3D tensor (x,y,RGB) | Histological slides |
| **3D** | Tensor voxels | CT, MRI |
| **4D** | Tensor voxels + time | fMRI, PET |

⚠️ Universal format: **DICOM** (data + patient metadata)

---

# Challenges in medical imaging

- Big images, **small datasets**
- Non-standardized acquisition
- **long-tail** distribution of diseases
- Labels **rare and noisy**
- **Heterogeneous and unbalanced** data
- Subjectivity in ground truth
- Anonymization sometimes impossible (e.g. facial scans)

---

# Learning Strategies

| Strategy | Data | Exit |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| **Supervised** | Patch-level labels | Direct local detection |
| **Semi-supervised** | Labels + non-labeled | Improved representation |
| **MIL** (Multi-Instance Learning) | Low image-level labels | Local + global detection |
| **Transfer Learning** | Domain A rich → Domain B poor | Cross-domain adaptation |

💡 **MIL**: positive bag if ≥ 1 positive instance → useful in anatomopathology

# Radiography (X-ray)

## Physical

$$E = h \cdot f = \frac{hc}{\lambda} \quad \Rightarrow E \sim \text{keV}$$

##3 photon-matter interactions

| Interaction | Mechanism | Imaging effect |
|-------------|-----------|----------------|
| **Photoelectric** | Total photon absorption | ✅ Desirable — forms contrast |
| **Compton** | Partial absorption, deviation | ⚠️ Noise (non-linear radius) |
| **Pair production** | E > 1.02 MeV, e⁻/e⁺ pair | Used in PET |

💡 Dense tissue (bone) → absorbs more → **white**. Air/muscle → absorbs less → **dark**

## Image quality — depends on

- Anode tip quality, patient thickness
- Phosphor, film resolution, sampling procedure
- Required resolution: **≥ 2000² pixels**

## Apps

| Application | Principle | Particularity |
|-------------|----------|---------------|
| **Fluoroscopy** | Real-time X-rays | Portable C-arm |
| **Angiography** | Iodine contrast IV | Invisible vessels without contrast |
| **DSA** | Pre-contrast mask subtraction | Replaced by CT Angiography |

# CT (Computed Tomography)

## History

| Year | Actor | Contribution |
|-------|--------|-------------|
| 1917 | Radon | Radon transform |
| 1963 | Cormack | Tomographic reconstruction analysis |
| 1972 | Hounsfield | 1st CT system |
| 1979 | Hounsfield + Cormack | Nobel Physiology/Medicine |

## Radon transform

$$p_\theta(r,\theta) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \mu(x,y)\,\delta(x\cos\theta + y\sin\theta - r)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y$$

- **Infinite projections** → perfect reconstruction
- In practice: **Filtered Back-Projection (FBP)**

## Beam geometries

| Type | Description | Usage |
|------|-------------|-------|
| **Parallel** | One source per department | Impractical |
| **Fan-beam** | Single source, 2D fan | Standard inspection |
| **Cone-beam** | 2D detector, one rotation | 3D Angiography |

## 3D Modalities

| Fashion | Principle | Characteristic |
|------|----------|----------------|
| **Single-slit** | Step-and-shoot | Simple, slow |
| **Helical** | Simultaneous table + rotation | Fast, pitch = TF/Δz |
| **Multislice** | Multiple rows of detectors | Near real time |
| **Cone-beam** | 1 single rotation | FDK reconstruction |

## Advantages / Disadvantages CT

| ✅ Benefits | ⚠️ Disadvantages |
|-------------|-----------------|
| No overlay | Moderate-high radiation |
| Multiplanar (axial/coronal/sagittal) | 47% collective medical dose (UK) |
| Non-invasive angiography | Contrast → renal risk, allergy |
| Fast, available | More expensive than x-ray |

# Nuclear Imaging

## Principle

1. Radiolabeled tracer (radionuclide) injection
2. Tracer → anatomical site with metabolic activity
3. Detection of emitted X-rays

💡 SNR much better than fMRI

## SPECT vs PET

| Criterion | SPECT | PET |
|---------|-------|-----|
| Photon | Single (collimator required) | γ pair at 180° |
| Resolution | 6–8mm | 2–3mm |
| Decay tracer | Slow | Fast |
| Tracer production | No on-site required | Cyclotron nearby |
| Cost | Cheaper | More expensive |
| Pictures | 64×64 or 128×128 px | — |

⚠️ SPECT: attenuation → **underestimation** in depth → correction by integrated CT

## PET — Mechanism

1. FDG (¹⁸F) injected
2. Decay → **positron emission**
3. Positron + electron → **annihilation** → 2 γ photons at 180°
4. Detection of coincident pairs only

Applications: oncology, cardiology, neurology

# MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging)

## Key story

| Year | Event |
|-------|-----------|
| 1946 | NMR demonstrated (Bloch + Purcell) |
| 1973 | 1st MRI image (Lauterbur) — Nobel 2003 |
| Early 1980s | 1st commercial systems |
| 1993 | fMRI in humans |

## Physical principle

$$\nu = \gamma |B_0| \quad (\text{fréquence de résonance})$$

For H: $\gamma = 42{,}58$ MHz/T

**Sequence**: $B_0$ aligns protons → RF pulse disturbs → return to equilibrium → signal captured

## Relaxations T1 and T2

| | T1 | T2 |
|-|----|----|
| Name | Spin-lattice relaxation | Spin-spin relaxation |
| Described | Return $M_z$ to equilibrium | Decay $M_{xy}$ |
| Formula | $M_z = M_0(1-e^{-t/T_1})$ | $M_{xy} = M_{xy0}\,e^{-t/T_2}$ |
| Relationship | — | **Always $T_2 \leq T_1$** |

💡 T1 and T2 are **tissue specific** → source of MRI contrast

## MRI modes

| Fashion | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Standard** | Multiple RF pulse sequences |
| **PPE** | Fast acquisition, fewer motion artifacts |
| **MRS** | Nuclei other than H (P, Na, F) |
| **fMRI** | BOLD contrast (blood oxygenation) |

## MRI applications

| Application | Principle | Use |
|-------------|----------|-------------|
| **MRA** | Paramagnetic / flow-related contrast | Stenosis, aneurysms |
| **MRS** | Fabric chemical spectrum | Cancer, epilepsy, Parkinson's |
| **fMRI** | BOLD (oxygenated/deoxygenated Hb) | Brain activity |
| **CDI** | MRI phase → current densities | Electrical mapping |
| **Interventional** | Procedure guidance | ~0.2 T → reduced sensitivity |

## MRI vs CT

| Criterion | CT | MRI |
|---------|----|----|
| Contrast | Attenuation T1, T2, density, flow… |
| Availability/cost | ✅ More available, cheaper | ❌ More expensive |
| Disbarment | ⚠️ Yes | ✅ No |
| Repetition | ⚠️ Cumulative Disbarment | ✅ Preferable |
| Bones/calcifications | ✅ Great | ❌ Less suitable |
| Soft tissues | Medium | ✅ Superior |
| Tumors | Less good | ✅ Generally superior |

# Ultrasound (Ultrasound Imaging)

## Physical properties

- **Longitudinal compression waves**
- Medical frequency: **> 2.5 MHz** (inaudible to humans)
- Piezoelectricity (Pierre Curie, 1880) → generation and detection

## Acquisition methods

| Fashion | Meaning | Principle | Usage |
|------|--------------|----------|-------|
| **A** | Amplitude | Simple echo, 1 line | Obsolete |
| **M** | Motion | A-repeated mode (1000 pulses/s) | Heart, fetus |
| **B** | Brightness | Translation/tilt transducer → 2D image | Standard |
| **CW Doppler** | Continuous Wave | Comparison $f_T$ vs $f_R$ | Continuous flow speed |
| **PW Doppler** | Pulsed Wave | Delayed signal, not strict Doppler | Flow location |

## CW Doppler formula

$$f_D = f_R - f_T \approx \frac{-2|v_a|\cos\theta}{c} f_T$$

## US Advantages / Disadvantages

| ✅ Benefits | ⚠️ Disadvantages |
|-------------|-----------------|
| Non-invasive, radiation-free | High speckle noise |
| Inexpensive, portable | Low spatial resolution |
| Real time (excellent $\Delta t$) | Depends on operator + anatomy |

---

# Critical points / Pitfalls ⚠️

- **Left/Right** in imaging = **patient** point of view (not observer)
- **Compton** → noise (not useful signal in radiography)
- **DSA** → replaced by CT angiography (less invasive)
- **SPECT** → attenuation underestimates activity at depth
- **PET** → fast decay tracers → nearby cyclotron required
- **$T_2 \leq T_1$** always
- **fMRI** → **indirect** signal (BOLD = oxygenation, not direct neuronal activity)
- **Cone-beam CT** → end sampling issues
- **Interventional MRI** → weak field (~0.2 T) → reduced sensitivity
- **CT** → 7% radiological examinations but **47% collective dose** (UK)
